names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Παυσίκακος Επίσκοπος Συνάδων», with the rank word and the see left off.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name link 1705 as the day page prints it, «Святитель Павсикакий (Павсакий) Синадский (Фригийский), епископ», with the rank words left off and the first of each pair kept. The calendar's own parentheses give a variant of the forename, Павсакий, and the province, Фригийский, beside the see; both are recorded here rather than in the form, which is `cyprian-martyr-10-may`'s precedent. The day's own line declines him «Свт. Павсикакия , еп. Синадского (ок. 606).» `fk.mjs` on «Павсикакий Синадский» returned NONE before the write.

death.note: **This replaces a bracket with the year inside it.** The folder carried «early 7th century», 595 to 620, which its own note described as what saint.gr's two reigns allowed, that page giving no year of death at all. days.pravoslavie.ru gives one in words — its life page closes «Святитель Павсикакий мирно скончался в 606 году» — and its day line prints «Свт. Павсикакия , еп. Синадского (ок. 606).» The same page has the patriarch Кириак (592–606) ordain him bishop of Synada and has him heal the emperor Маврикий (582–602) at Constantinople, so 606 sits at the end of one reign and after the other, and contradicts neither. No birth is recorded: the page says only that he lived «в конце VI века в Сирийском городе Апамее» and was brought up in the faith by pious parents, and a youth placed in a century is not a year.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 мая ст. ст. — «Свт. Павсикакия , еп. Синадского (ок. 606).»

attestations.note: The same menologion day the folder already keeps for the Greek, and the same man: the bishop of Synada with the gift of healing who cured the emperor Маврикий at Constantinople and brought water out of the ground for his thirsty companions on the road home. **`dates` were replaced, narrowed and not widened.** The folder carried «early 7th century», 595 to 620, a bracket its own note says was built out of the two reigns saint.gr names because that page gives no year; the Russian life page says «Святитель Павсикакий мирно скончался в 606 году» and the day line prints «(ок. 606)». 606 falls inside the bracket it replaces, and it is also the last year of the patriarch Кириак (592–606) whom the same page has ordain him, so the two sources do not contradict. The Russian adds Апамея in Syria for his birthplace and the end of the sixth century for his youth; **no `locations` were recorded**, because the folder has a see in its `office` already and the page gives no more than city names. The day page prints hymns for three of the saints it heads and nothing under his name. azbyka.ru was not read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Παυσίκακος Επίσκοπος Συνάδων»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **Nothing in the corpus reads as him**: the namesweep printed no row for the name at all. **`physician` is in `types`** on the page's own «σπούδασε όχι μόνο Θεολογία, αλλά και ιατρική για να την εξασκήσει δωρεάν υπέρ των φτωχών» — he studied medicine to practise it free for the poor — and on the emperor Maurice's cure. **The `dates` bracket is the page's own two reigns and nothing else**, and its `note` says so; the page gives no year of birth or death. **No `locations` object**, although Apamea in Bithynia and Synada are named. No hymn is printed; the page's couplet promises a strange ceasing of ills to whoever runs to his relic.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
